claim_findings.passage: CFO said margin will always be diluted by inflation, particularly fuel price inflation, flowing through the P&L this year.
claim_findings.evidence: Read in the full segment context. Immediately before the quoted CFO remark, the CEO says in the same answer: "Clearly, to deliver Retail operating profit growth year-on-year we expect to deliver a positive margin outcome", and the CFO's own next sentence is "we will make balanced choices as we travel". The extracted claim isolates the dilution half of a two-sided answer, so a reader of claims.json alone sees only the negative margin signal. This is what the outlook brief then builds its base case on.
claim_findings.recommendation: Extend claim_text to preserve the balancing statement (management expects a positive margin outcome despite inflation dilution), or add a companion claim capturing the positive-margin expectation from the same segment.

claim_findings.passage: General Merchandise + Clothing sales fell 3.7% YoY to £438m.
claim_findings.evidence: The claim set records the GM+Clothing decline but never records management's own stated cause for it, even though it is stated twice in this run's evidence. The prepared remarks say GM "sales were impacted by some seasonal weakness but more significantly by our ongoing and planned programme to tighten ranges and reduce space allocation in favour of food", and web-013 says GM sales were "down (6.3) per cent, primarily reflecting an ongoing programme to focus General Merchandise ranges more tightly and reduce space allocation in favour of food". Neither statement, nor the separate GM (6.3)% and Tu Clothing (2.1)% split, is captured anywhere in claims.json. Its absence is the direct cause of the high-severity mischaracterisation in outlook-brief.md sections 1 and 4.
claim_findings.recommendation: Add a claim from the prepared-remarks segment (and/or web-013) capturing management's primary stated attribution of the GM decline to the planned space-reduction programme, plus the GM-only (6.3)% figure.

outlook_findings.passage: a distinction management's own framing on the call blurred by attributing GM softness mainly to "seasonal weakness" [claim-002] before disclosing the space-reallocation programme only later, in Q&A [claim-018]
outlook_findings.evidence: Three separate problems in one sentence, and the same error is repeated in section 1 ("a sharper decline than management's framing on the call (\"some seasonal weakness\" [claim-002]) suggested in isolation"). First, the citation is wrong: claim-002 is "Grocery sales grew 3.6% YoY to £7,603m", quote "| Grocery | 3.6% | 7,603 |" -- it contains no reference to seasonal weakness at all, so a quoted phrase is attached to a claim id that does not carry it. Second, the factual assertion is contradicted by the transcript: in the prepared remarks, before any Q&A, the CEO says GM "sales were impacted by some seasonal weakness but more significantly by our ongoing and planned programme to tighten ranges and reduce space allocation in favour of food" -- management named the space programme as the larger driver, in the opening statement, not "only later, in Q&A". Third, web-013 in this run's own evidence pack says GM sales were down "(6.3) per cent, primarily reflecting an ongoing programme to ... reduce space allocation in favour of food", so the same-day results release also led with the space programme. The brief therefore levels a disclosure-quality criticism at management that its own cited evidence refutes.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Delete the claim that management blurred the distinction or disclosed the space programme only in Q&A. Replace it with the accurate reading (management attributed the GM decline primarily to the planned space reduction in both the prepared remarks and the results release), cite a claim that actually carries that attribution once one exists, and remove the [claim-002] citation from both sections.

outlook_findings.passage: both segments beat the pre-event Shore Capital consensus range [claim-026][claim-027], a clean positive surprise on the headline volume story
outlook_findings.evidence: The two beats are real, but the framing is one-sided against evidence sitting in this run's own pack. web-014 (Hargreaves Lansdown, same day) records GM+Clothing at -3.7% against -1.3% expected -- a miss roughly as large as the Argos beat -- and describes ex-fuel sales growth of 2.7% as "in line with market expectations", i.e. the headline was not a surprise at all. web-013's own five-quarter table shows total Sainsbury's growth decelerating 4.9% -> 5.5% -> 4.9% -> 4.3% -> 3.1% and like-for-like ex-fuel decelerating 4.6% -> 4.3% -> 3.4% -> 3.1% -> 2.1%, the slowest in five quarters. claim-005 (2.7% total retail ex-fuel) and claim-006 (2.1% LFL) exist in claims.json and are never cited anywhere in the brief.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Qualify the "clean positive surprise" framing: state that the two segment beats sat alongside a GM+Clothing miss and an in-line, five-quarter-low headline growth rate, and cite claim-005 and claim-006 where the headline is discussed.

outlook_findings.passage: plausible given inflation already "stepped back" in Q1 versus Q4 and management noted trade bodies "adjusting down" their own inflation estimates during the call

I confirmed all three phrases do appear in raw/transcript.txt, so they are not fabricated, but they were never extracted into claims.json and therefore never passed the exact-quote gate that every other quotation in this pipeline goes through. The load-bearing evidence for the entire upside case is the least verified material in the document.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Extract the inflation-trajectory commentary (Q1 inflation stepping back versus Q4, trade bodies adjusting estimates down) as claims and cite them, or drop the direct quotations and state the point in the brief's own words as author interpretation.

outlook_findings.passage: enough to keep the FY profit outcome inside the guided range but closer to the middle than the "upper end" language in claim-011 implies
outlook_findings.evidence: Two problems. First, this is a positioning judgment about where the outcome falls inside £975m-£1,075m, which section 9 of the same document explicitly refuses to make: "This brief does not treat these as the same metric or compute where £1,045m sits within £975m-£1,075m". The base case does exactly what section 9 disclaims. Second, the cited support (claim-019, claim-021) is entirely qualitative -- neither quantifies any margin impact -- so nothing in the evidence sizes the headwind well enough to move the outcome from "upper end" to "middle". Counterevidence in the same transcript segment as claim-019, where the CEO says "to deliver Retail operating profit growth year-on-year we expect to deliver a positive margin outcome", is not surfaced or rebutted.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Either state the base case as directional (margin headwinds temper the upper-end framing) without asserting a position within the range, or remove the section 9 disclaimer and argue the positioning explicitly with evidence that sizes the headwind. Also surface management's positive-margin expectation as the counterargument.

summary: Fail, on one high-severity finding. Outlook-brief.md sections 1 and 4 accuse management of blurring the cause of the General Merchandise decline and of disclosing the space-reallocation programme "only later, in Q&A". Both the transcript's prepared remarks and web-013 in this run's own evidence pack show management named the planned space reduction as the more significant driver up front, and the quoted phrase "seasonal weakness" is cited to claim-002, which is the grocery sales figure and contains no such wording. Three medium outlook findings follow a common thread: the brief is more confident than its evidence in both directions -- a one-sided "clean positive surprise" framing that ignores the GM+Clothing miss and the five-quarter-low headline growth visible in its own cited source, an upside case resting on three uncited direct quotations that never passed the quote gate, and a base-case positioning judgment that the brief's own section 9 disclaims. On the claims side, the extraction captured the beats but not the misses, and isolated the dilution half of a two-sided CFO answer on margin. Deterministic stages all passed and are confirmed present; the injection scan is genuinely clean; sources opened were authentic and correctly dated. Sector language is appropriate throughout -- grocery, general merchandise, loyalty and retail media, with no template metrics borrowed from another industry.
proposed_lessons: Every quoted phrase in the outlook brief must appear in the quote of the claim cited beside it; never attach a transcript quotation to a claim id that does not contain it.

Before describing a segment's decline as demand weakness or criticising how management framed it, check the prepared remarks and the results release for management's own primary stated cause and extract it as a claim.
When extracting pre-event expectations, capture the metrics the company missed as well as the ones it beat, so the brief cannot present a selective beat as a clean surprise.
